verses.text: I made a covenant with my eyes. How could I look at a young woman with lust?
What share would God above give me? What would I inherit from the Almighty on high?
Doesn’t ruin fall on the unrighteous and disaster on people who do wrong?
Doesn’t God see how I live and count every step I take?
If I’ve lived a lie or rushed to deceive anyone,
let God weigh me on honest scales so he can see my integrity.
If I’ve strayed from the right path, let my heart chase what my eyes wanted, or let any wrongdoing stick to my hands,
then let someone else eat what I plant, and let my crops be pulled up by the roots.
If another woman has drawn my heart away and I’ve waited in secret at my neighbor’s door,
then let my wife grind grain for another man, and let other men sleep with her.
That would be a shameful crime, an offense for judges to punish.
It would be a fire that burns everything to ruin and uproots all I’ve gained.
If I brushed aside the complaint of a man or woman who worked for me when they brought a case against me,
what would I do when God rises to judge? What could I say when he calls me to account?
Didn’t the same God who made me in the womb make them too? Didn’t one God form us both?
If I kept the poor from getting what they needed or made a widow lose hope,
or if I ate my food alone and gave none to the fatherless,
though since my youth I raised the fatherless like a father and guided widows from my earliest days,
if I saw anyone dying for lack of clothes or saw a needy person with nothing to wear,
and they had no reason to bless me because I never warmed them with the wool from my sheep,
or if I raised my hand against the fatherless because I knew I had allies at the city gate,
then let my shoulder come out of its socket and my arm snap at the joint.
Disaster from God terrifies me. Before his majesty I can do nothing.
If I put my hope in gold and told pure gold, ‘You’re what I count on,’
if I took pride in how rich I was and how much I’d gained by my own hand,
if I saw the sun shining or the moon moving in splendor,
and my heart was secretly drawn to them and I blew them a kiss,
that too would be an offense for judges to punish, because I would have denied God above.
If I celebrated when someone who hated me was ruined or gloated when trouble found them,
though I never let my mouth sin by cursing them and asking for their life,
or if the people in my tent couldn’t say, ‘Can you find anyone who hasn’t had their fill of his food?’
though I opened my doors to travelers so strangers didn’t have to sleep in the street,
if I covered up my wrongs like Adam and hid my guilt in my heart,
because I was afraid of the crowd and terrified of what families might think, so I stayed quiet and never went outside,
if only someone would hear me! Here’s my signature. Let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser write down the charges!
I’d carry that document on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
I’d account for every step I’ve taken. I’d approach him like a prince.
If my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
if I’ve eaten what it produced without paying or caused its owners to lose their lives,
then let thornbushes grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley. Job’s words end here.
